title: Measurement Trail: hash-chained provenance records for measurement processing steps
description:
Measurement Trail records the provenance of a measurement as it moves through device and software processing steps. Each event (timestamp, step, actor, optional metadata and payload digest) is stored as one canonical JSON line with a sequence number, the previous record's hash and its own SHA-256 record hash. Payloads are referenced by digest only. The append command verifies the existing trail before writing and holds an advisory file lock on Linux and macOS; the verify command checks schema, canonical encoding, sequence and hash links.

Scope: this is an integrity check, not tamper-proof storage. Records are unsigned, so authorship is not authenticated, and removal of trailing records cannot be detected without independently stored checkpoints. It says nothing about sensor accuracy or calibration.

Usage: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only; pip install . adds a measurement-trail command. Run python3 measurement_trail.py verify samples/example.jsonl. Tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v (run in CI on Python 3.10 to 3.13 with coverage).

Citation: cite the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23067465 for all versions, or the version DOI of the release you used. Source code: github.com/sparkainlp-x/measurement-trail. Licence: AGPL-3.0-only; commercial licensing is available (see COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md).
notes: Evidence status: SYNTHETIC example data; no field performance is claimed. Commercial licensing: see COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md.
